Although all key project leads provide input for the runbook to the service management team, the primary roles in creating the runbook are the project manager, business process team lead, and the technical team lead.

When implementing a commercial solution, a vendor will typically provide a checklist for cutover preparation that can be modified to fit the organization's specific needs. This checklist should not be considered a replacement for the organization’s runbook creation process, but is a key input.

The piloting process, among other goals, will uncover any issues which would affect the transition cutover process. Once the implementation completes the pilot phase and resulting updates are made, there will be less likelihood of a “no-go” decision being made.

The cutover runbook outlines the steps to be completed to verify the organization is ready for operational use of the new solution.

The runbook documents system cutover activities in the appropriate sequence to verfiy preparatory steps are complete and that the right people have reviewed the plan, agree with the contents, are ready to use it, and available when required.

The runbook details specific tasks which verify the operation of the implementation goals in the operational environment once a go/no-go decision has been provided. Completion of the technology runbook items assures that all required data is migrated and verified, all users are prepared for production, the replaced system(s) are removed from the production environment or otherwise accounted for, and initial post-transition business and technology-related processes are scheduled.

Preparation for the cutover covers all aspects of the implementation with adequate time allocations and support resource availability. Prior to the cutover, the implementation build should be tested to make sure it is complete and components verified by IT and the business. This can be done in a pilot release depending on the implementation complexity. All application interfaces should pass testing for any connectivity and compatibility issues. Backup and downtime procedures should also be checked.

While some of this will be part of operations the actual scheduling of the initial processes should be done as part of the transition.

Proper staff training is a critical step in the cutover process. This training includes technical and procedural aspects. As the cutover event arrives, proper communication to IT and business should be verified so all parties have been given proper notification. Once the checklist items have been satisfied and a go / no-go decision has been made, the implementation is ready to proceed into the production environment with live production data.

Element.attribute: Execute manual configuration tasks in production environment
Execute manual configuration tasks in production environment

Configuration is the setting of various conditions and states that enables the system to perform according to the proposed design. While many configuration objects can be moved between different environments automatically via transports, patches, or the like, some configuration objects must be manually configured in each environment. Therefore, one of the steps of cutover is to perform the manual steps in the production environment. This should be done in adherence with the configuration documentation developed during the solution design, build, and test phases.

Execute configuration steps in the production environment if they can't be transported or automatically created. Verify that all configuration objects are properly implemented so that the production environment will behave as designed.

  • Identify manual configuration objects
  • Review configuration rationale for the object
  • Review identified configuration values
  • Request configuration access to production environment (firefighter or cutover ID)
  • Update manual configuration objects
  • Update project plan

Configuration should be done in adherence with the configuration documentation developed during the solution design, build, and test phases.

A checklist should be used to verify all manual configuration steps in production have been executed and are ready for cutover. This checklist will be a resource for project or workstream management. The steps in the checklist may include:

  • Validation that parent configuration tasks are complete
  • Validation that manual configuration entries have been executed
  • Validation of manual configuration entries

Element.attribute: Transfer configuration and settings to production environment
Transfer configuration and settings to production environment

Implementing a documented and methodical process for moving all of the configurations and settings into the production environment avoids issues with missing transports, transports failing to integrate properly, or other potentially disruptive issues.

Transfer all manual and automated configuration settings into the production environment in the correct sequence. Confirm that the production environment is properly configured for successful operation and behaves in the same manner during all development and testing phases.

  • Validate precursor documentation
  • Document the proper transport sequence
  • Validate of presence of transports in the pre-production environment
  • Execute manual and automatic transports
  • Test and validate configurations and settings in the production environment

It is critical not only to validate that all transports are moved, but that all are integrated in the proper sequence. Many transports or settings have precursors (either manual or automatic) that must be implemented prior to their own integration. If not done in the proper sequence, the solution may function incorrectly, if at all.

Documenting the configuration and settings to transfer also serves as an excellent means of knowledge transfer, as it is an entry point to begin educating site deployment team members or new project team members on how the solution is configured and how it will behave.

Element.attribute: Perform test run of critical production processes
Perform test run of critical production processes

Simulate or execute critical production processes to verify a working and usable system. Provide additional assurance that critical production processes will operate as expected in production.

By doing the critical production test as accurately as possible, the team can be as certain as possible when entering go-live that critical defects that could disrupt the business will be avoided.

Confirm that all critical processes have been listed and remove from the test plan any processes that are not valid for specified deployment

Schedule test processes, making sure to account for operational up and down time as needed as well as resource availability for both deployment teams and operational personnel

  • Assign team members responsible for overseeing tests
  • Execute and track tests against test plan, logging defects as necessary
  • Confirm that all defects which may cause failures in critical production processes have been resolved

Once all tests have been executed, all applicable defects closed, notify project and site management of completion of the test. If possible, use the actual production system to perform the tests, as production will best replicate the actual behavior of cutover and go-live. If that is not feasible, use the pre-production (i.e., simulation) environment; this may be the best possible emulation, as long as it is validated that the pre-production environment is a true carbon copy of the production system. Any differences in patches, transports, etc., can result in the test being misinterpreted.

A particular integration, interface, or function may result in major disruption to operations if there are any issues. For example, a manufacturing facility may have a solution interfaced with a work order system that authorizes the operation of CNC machines. If the interface does not work, a machine on the floor may not receive the required data and may not work. If this is an issue affecting the interface as a whole, it is highly likely that the entire operation may shut down until this is resolved.

Activate and monitor all batch jobs for required automated system processing. Begin business as usual (BAU) batch processing and confirm that any incidents or problems are quickly discovered and addressed.

  • Verify that the configuration required for batch jobs (processes and report) in the system as defined. Batch job configuration is initiated as part of system configuration and will be updated until go-live.
  • Verify security and access required for batch jobs are correctly set up in the production environment and that roles are loaded to restrict and control access to the system.
  • Activate all batch jobs for automated system processing.
  • Monitor the activated batch jobs and communicate the performance, error resolution and plan of risk mitigation for critical errors to the project team.

Identify and document batch network startup sequence

Batch jobs are essential and a critical part of project implementation. Several jobs with large volumes of data require automated batch jobs to be set up. There are several other subsequent activities defined as part of cutover plan is dependent on these jobs being executed successfully.

The batch schedule defines certain time intervals when the batch jobs should be executed and that contains schedules for batch jobs requiring daily, weekly, monthly and annual automation.

This step is one of the action items as part of cutover plan and is usually executed after the roles and access required for batch jobs are set up.
